claims.summary: For alpha_1, alpha_2 in (0,infinity] with 1/alpha_1+1/alpha_2<1/2 and every fixed L>0, for X i.i.d. uniform on [0,1]^2 and Y either evenly spread or an independent uniform sample, with probability tending to one no matching satisfies sum_i exp[(sqrt N|X_i^j-Y^j_pi(i)|/(L sqrt(log N)))^alpha_j] <= 2N (maximum bound L sqrt(log N/N) at infinity) for both j=1,2. So the ultimate matching conjecture cannot be strengthened below its curve at any pair, in either setting; e.g. (alpha,infinity) fails for every alpha>2.
claims.assessment: Working proof: the vertically scaled Leighton-Shor subgraph of Step 1 of lem:leighton-shor-class-lower-bound with kappa=(log N)^(1/alpha_2-1/alpha_1), crossing pairs bounded by an anisotropic boundary layer counted on a grid of side L sqrt(log N/N) plus at most two long displacements; the exponents balance exactly on the curve. A direct adaptation of the monograph's proof of Theorem 4.8.1; neither source read states it; no novelty claimed.
claims.rationale: Shows the conjecture cannot be strengthened at any pair below its curve, in both settings and for every constant.
claims.next_action: None for sharpness; the open part of the conjecture is the upper bound on the curve.
